question: The Aarhus Convention Compliance Committee initiated proceedings1 concerning the Commission’s failure to comply with the right of access to environmental information, the latter having rejected a request concerning the San Finx mine in Galicia.

The request concerned, inter alia, three documents on the NEXT project, financed by the Commission, which resulted in illegal discharges of contaminated water, as well as a restoration project carried out illegally in 2020. On 20 February 2024, the Commission (ENV.E4) intervened before the Aarhus Convention Compliance Committee requesting that the complaint be declared inadmissible.

To that end, the Commission argued that resorting to the European Ombudsman did not constitute a valid avenue for challenging the Commission’s decisions and that only a procedure before the General Court would allow for a subsequent complaint before the Committee. 1.

Does the Commission consider that complaints to the European Ombudsman concerning breaches of the right of access to environmental information are not a valid means of redress for decisions on environmental information?
Will the Commission modify its opinion on the non-admissibility of complaint ACCC/C/2024/207, and thus allow the facts to be investigated?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) The Commission is fully aware of the important role of the European Ombudsman as one of the means of redress under Regulation 1049/2001 on public access to documents of the EU institutions.

The Ombudsman offers an alternative non-judicial remedy on alleged instances of maladministration but cannot make a legally binding decision on an alleged breach of the Aarhus Convention1 and the respective implementing legislation at the EU level. Only the EU courts have this role.
Therefore, filing a complaint with the Ombudsman cannot be considered as exhausting the domestic remedies to submit a communication to the Aarhus Convention Compliance Committee (ACCC).

In the Commission’s view, the ACCC should take into account that the applicant has to address the General Court to obtain an effective and sufficient mean of redress regarding the interpretation and implementation of respective EU legislation. The ACCC should not become a parallel means of redress. The Commission notes that the ACCC has already accepted the preliminary admissibility of this case.

The Commission will still submit its observations, both on admissibility and on substance. The NEXT Research & Innovation project, no. 776804 had activities of ore sampling from 21 January to 1 February 2019 and from 6 to 8 August 2019. Thus, the Commission does not know what the relation is to the ‘restoration project carried out illegally in 2020’.

Furthermore, the Commission did not receive any relevant evidence, in particular administrative decisions and/or court rulings by the respective national authorities confirming allegations on water discharge and/or its relation to the NEXT project.
